# tfutils_aws_eni_released_wait (Resource)

Creates nothing. On destroy, waits until the VPC has no amazon-vpc-cni ENI of the cluster that is `available` or whose attachment is `detaching`, that is, until vpc-cni finishes releasing the ENIs it detached. Destroy fails with the remaining ENIs when the delete timeout passes. Make this resource depend on the resources whose deletion terminates the nodes, and the workloads on those nodes depend on this resource.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tfutils_aws_eni_released_wait" "vpc_cni" {
  vpc_id       = var.vpc_id
  cluster_name = var.cluster_name

  timeouts {
    delete = "10m"
  }

  depends_on = [kubectl_manifest.nodepool]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_name` (String) Value of the `cluster.k8s.amazonaws.com/name` tag that vpc-cni puts on the cluster's ENIs.
- `vpc_id` (String) VPC of the cluster.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<vpc_id>/<cluster_name>`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
